extracted.intended_audience: legislators, legislative staff, civic technologists, potential partners and funders
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and standards for designing, prototyping, and deploying civic-technology products and policy work for legislatures, emphasizing user-centered research, rapid prototyping, open source, and policy change. Aimed at teams working with Members of Congress, staff, and constituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apolitical nonprofit commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The OpenGov Foundation describes itself as a 'fiercely apolitical nonprofit dedicated to serving those who serve the people in America’s legislatures.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects and engagement should maintain an apolitical stance focused on serving legislative institutions and the public rather than partisan advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: enable meaningful, scalable engagement and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a 21st century Congress where elected officials and staff can meaningfully engage at scale with those they represent, and where citizens can see, shape, and understand the critical decisions that affect their lives, their families, and their businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design outcomes should improve both the scale and quality of engagement and increase transparency so constituents can understand and influence legislative decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-centered research: understand users before building
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you solve a problem, you must first understand the challenge and the people facing it. Before we build, we walk many miles in our users’ shoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in deep user research (observations, interviews, contextual inquiry) to ground problem definitions; avoid designing solutions without first understanding real user needs and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid prototyping and direct user testing
rubrics_metrics.description: With a solid understanding of a problem, we rapidly design, prototype, and test products and services directly with Members, staff, and constituents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer quick, testable prototypes and demos over long written plans. 'We believe in demos, not memos.' Use iterative prototypes to validate assumptions with target users early and often; avoid launching untested, polished documents as substitutes for working demos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterate as true partners and aggressively measure results
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything starts with those who serve and those they represent. We fall in love with their problems, rapidly prototype improvements, iterate as true partners, then aggressively measure the results. Lather. Rinse. Repeat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work in close partnership with stakeholders, use iterative cycles, and apply rigorous measurement to evaluate impact; measurement should inform subsequent iterations and demonstrate value to partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build and promote open source products
rubrics_metrics.description: Founded within the halls of Congress and launched in 2013, we and our open source products have supported more than 50 communities, states, and countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor open source tooling and practices to enable reuse, transparency, and community adoption; share code and learnings so others can adapt and scale solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy work must enable efficient, effective, accountable action
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and development isn’t enough. Our legislatures need modern policies to support efficient, effective, and accountable action. We’re a trusted policy voice on issues from open source software to creating a Congressional Digital Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement technical solutions with policy recommendations that institutionalize improvements; aim for policies that increase efficiency, effectiveness, and accountability in legislative processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grow the community and foster market entry and competition
rubrics_metrics.description: An effective Congress needs greater choice and competition in the marketplace. We share what we learn and invest our time and resources to help others building world-class products and services enter the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively share knowledge and support other teams and vendors to broaden the ecosystem; treat ecosystem growth as a success metric and avoid hoarding expertise or creating closed monopolies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empower through technology, data, and human-centered design
rubrics_metrics.description: We empower those who serve in our democracy with better technology, data, and human-centered design. Everyone wins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine technical solutions, data tools, and user-centered design to create practical, usable systems for legislative users; measure success by improvements experienced by both staff and constituents.
